newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-WEARY FOURSOME BATTLE INTO RECORD BOOKS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-WEARY FOURSOME BATTLE INTO RECORD BOOKS.

text.p: Four exhausted doubles players entered their names in the Australian Open record books on Wednesday, compiling the longest set in the event's history before an Australian men's pair finally prevailed 29-27.

The first round match, played on an obscure outside court in a remote corner of the sprawling Melbourne Park venue, dragged on for over seven hours, including rain breaks, before Jon Ireland and Wayne Arthurs trudged off the court triumphant.
"That was the most exciting match I have ever played in my life," Ireland told reporters as he and his partner headed for the massage table.
The local pair beat Italians Cristian Brandi and Filippo Messori 6-3 3-6 29-27, eclipsing the old Australian Open men's doubles record set of 23-21 in 1990.

Though Wednesday's match went for four hours and 36 minutes' playing time, it fell well short of the world record for the longest doubles match of 147 games -- won 3-6 49-47 22-20 in an all-American marathon at a 1967 invitational at Newport, Rhode Island.
"We didn't want it to go that long. I was starting to get a little tired," 30-year-old Ireland, who is playing his last year on tour, said after being told of the Rhode Island marathon.
Ireland's girlfriend Julie Evans, one of only about five spectators when play began, was also tiring as a hushed capacity crowd gathered to witness the final points.
"I didn't think it was ever going to end," she said.
